Warning: The Dockerfile runs an editable install without dependency resolution and without pinning the project package:
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --no-deps -e .
Why this is an issue: --no-deps causes pip to skip installing any dependency metadata declared by the project; if the earlier explicit pinned pip installs do not fully cover the project's required dependencies, the container build may produce a broken runtime. Also pip install -e . does not pin a specific version of the project package itself; the rubric requires installed packages and tools to be explicitly pinned for reproducibility. Recommended fixes: either install the project from a pinned package or install dependencies from a pinned requirements file or lockfile (e.g., use a committed requirements.txt with == pins or use the project's lockfile); remove --no-deps unless you intentionally manage all dependencies elsewhere.

Warning: The Dockerfile fetches external git repositories at build time (network fetch) even though the fetches are pinned to commits:
RUN set -e; \
    fetch() { \
      if [ ! -f "$1/$4" ]; then \
        rm -rf "$1" && git init -q "$1" \
          && git -C "$1" fetch -q --depth 1 "$2" "$3" \
          && git -C "$1" checkout -q FETCH_HEAD \
          && rm -rf "$1/.git"; \
      fi; \
    }; \
    fetch jedi/third_party/typeshed https://github.com/davidhalter/typeshed.git \
      4bb9d8351d0795fbc7dee3da069013a48641689d LICENSE; \
    fetch jedi/third_party/django-stubs https://github.com/davidhalter/django-stubs.git \
      fd057010f6cbf176f57d1099e82be46d39b99cb9 LICENSE.txt
Why this is an issue: While the fetches are pinned to specific commit SHAs (which is good for reproducibility), build-time network fetches require network access and the presence of git in the build image. If the build environment is air-gapped or the base image does not include git, this RUN will fail. It also increases build time and external dependency surface. Recommended fixes: vendor these submodules into the repository (so COPY . . includes them), ensure git is present in the build image, or document that network access is required for docker build. If keeping the fetch approach, the pinned SHAs mitigate non-determinism (good).

+"""
+Choosing the overload of a function from the arguments of a call.
+"""
+
+from textwrap import dedent
+
+import pytest
+
+HEADER = """\
+from typing import overload, Any, Type, TypeVar, Union
+
+class A: pass
+class B(A): pass
+class C: pass
+class RA: pass
+class RB: pass
+class RC: pass
+"""
+
+
+def overloads(*annotations):
+    code = ''
+    for annotation, result in zip(annotations, ('RA', 'RB', 'RC')):
+        code += '@overload\ndef f(x: %s) -> %s: ...\n' % (annotation, result)
+    return code + 'def f(x): ...\n'
+
+
+def infer_result(Script, code):
+    code = HEADER + dedent(code).strip('\n')
+    lines = code.splitlines()
+    return sorted(d.name for d in Script(code).infer(len(lines), len(lines[-1])))
+
+
+def check(Script, annotations, call, expected, prefix=''):
+    code = prefix + overloads(*annotations) + call
+    assert infer_result(Script, code) == expected, (annotations, call)
+
+
+def test_issue_example(Script):
+    code = dedent('''\
+        from typing import overload
+
+        class Foo: pass
+
+        class FooBuilder:
+            def func_foo(self): pass
+
+        class Bar: pass
+
+        class BarBuilder:
+            def func_bar(self): pass
+
+        @overload
+        def get_obj(input: type[Foo]) -> FooBuilder: ...
+        @overload
+        def get_obj(input: type[Bar]) -> BarBuilder: ...
+        def get_obj(input: type): pass
+
+        builder = get_obj(Foo)
+        builder.''')
+    names = [c.name for c in Script(code).complete()]
+    assert 'func_foo' in names
+    assert 'func_bar' not in names
+
+    code = code.replace('get_obj(Foo)', 'get_obj(Bar)')
+    names = [c.name for c in Script(code).complete()]
+    assert 'func_bar' in names
+    assert 'func_foo' not in names
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('first', ['type[A]', 'Type[A]'])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    'call, expected', [
+        ('f(A)', ['RA']),
+        ('f(B)', ['RA']),
+        ('f(C)', ['RB']),
+    ]
+)
+def test_type_of_class(Script, first, call, expected):
+    check(Script, [first, 'type[C]'], call, expected)
+
+
+def test_type_rejects_instances(Script):
+    check(Script, ['type[A]', 'A'], 'f(A())', ['RB'])
+    check(Script, ['Type[A]', 'A'], 'f(B())', ['RB'])
+    check(Script, ['A', 'type[A]'], 'f(A)', ['RB'])
+    factory = 'class Factory:\n    def __call__(self) -> A: ...\n'
+    check(Script, ['type[A]', 'Factory'], 'f(Factory())', ['RB'], prefix=factory)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('annotation', ['type', 'Type', 'type[Any]', 'Type[Any]'])
+def test_any_class(Script, annotation):
+    check(Script, ['int', annotation], 'f(C)', ['RB'])
+    check(Script, [annotation, 'int'], 'f(3)', ['RB'])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('annotation', ['type[Union[A, C]]', 'Type[A | C]', 'type[A] | type[C]'])
+def test_type_of_union(Script, annotation):
+    check(Script, ['int', annotation], 'f(C)', ['RB'])
+    check(Script, ['int', annotation], 'f(B)', ['RB'])
+
+
+def test_type_of_type_var(Script):
+    bound = 'T = TypeVar("T", bound=A)\n'
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'int'], 'f(C)', ['RA', 'RB'], prefix=bound)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(C)', ['RB'], prefix=bound)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(B)', ['RA'], prefix=bound)
+    constrained = 'T = TypeVar("T", A, int)\n'
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(C)', ['RB'], prefix=constrained)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(int)', ['RA'], prefix=constrained)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(B)', ['RA'], prefix=constrained)
+    unbound = 'T = TypeVar("T")\n'
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'type[C]'], 'f(C)', ['RA'], prefix=unbound)
+    check(Script, ['type[T]', 'int'], 'f(3)', ['RB'], prefix=unbound)
+
+

+Choosing the overload of a function from the arguments of a call.
+"""
+
+from textwrap import dedent
+
+import pytest
+
+HEADER = """\
+from typing import overload, Any, Type, TypeVar, Union
+
+class A: pass
+class B(A): pass
+class C: pass
+class RA: pass
+class RB: pass
+class RC: pass
+"""
+
+
+def overloads(*annotations):
+    code = ''
+    for annotation, result in zip(annotations, ('RA', 'RB', 'RC')):
+        code += '@overload\ndef f(x: %s) -> %s: ...\n' % (annotation, result)
+    return code + 'def f(x): ...\n'
+
+
+def infer_result(Script, code):
+    code = HEADER + dedent(code).strip('\n')
+    lines = code.splitlines()
+    return sorted(d.name for d in Script(code).infer(len(lines), len(lines[-1])))
+
+
+def check(Script, annotations, call, expected, prefix=''):
+    code = prefix + overloads(*annotations) + call
+    assert infer_result(Script, code) == expected, (annotations, call)
+
+
+def test_issue_example(Script):
+    code = dedent('''\
+        from typing import overload
+
+        class Foo: pass
+
+        class FooBuilder:
+            def func_foo(self): pass
+
+        class Bar: pass
+
+        class BarBuilder:
+            def func_bar(self): pass
+
+        @overload
+        def get_obj(input: type[Foo]) -> FooBuilder: ...
+        @overload
+        def get_obj(input: type[Bar]) -> BarBuilder: ...
+        def get_obj(input: type): pass
+
+        builder = get_obj(Foo)
+        builder.''')
+    names = [c.name for c in Script(code).complete()]
+    assert 'func_foo' in names
+    assert 'func_bar' not in names
+
+    code = code.replace('get_obj(Foo)', 'get_obj(Bar)')
+    names = [c.name for c in Script(code).complete()]
+    assert 'func_bar' in names
+    assert 'func_foo' not in names
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('first', ['type[A]', 'Type[A]'])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    'call, expected', [
+        ('f(A)', ['RA']),
+        ('f(B)', ['RA']),
+        ('f(C)', ['RB']),
+    ]
+)

+

+    check(Script, ['Type[A]', 'A'], 'f(B())', ['RB'])
+    check(Script, ['A', 'type[A]'], 'f(A)', ['RB'])
+    factory = 'class Factory:\n    def __call__(self) -> A: ...\n'
+    check(Script, ['type[A]', 'Factory'], 'f(Factory())', ['RB'], prefix=factory)

tests.verifies: With overloads `type[A]`/`Type[A]` then `type[C]`, the inferred result is `RA` for `f(A)` and `f(B)`, and `RB` for `f(C)`.

tests.evidence: The prompt states that `type[X]` accepts the class and subclasses, not instances, and conversely an ordinary `X` parameter does not accept the class `X` itself.
tests.name: test_type_rejects_instances
tests.qualityCheck: Covers both directions of class-versus-instance distinction, including an instance produced by a callable. The four cases are useful controls rather than one isolated example.
tests.verifies: The four calls infer `RB`: `f(A())` and `f(B())` choose the ordinary `A` overload over `type[A]`; `f(A)` chooses `type[A]` over ordinary `A`; and `f(Factory())` chooses `Factory` over `type[A]`.

tests.evidence: The prompt explicitly says unparameterized `type`/`Type` and `type[Any]` accept any class, while the earlier stated class-object rule distinguishes classes from instances. `Type[Any]` is the tested spelling of the same annotation family.
tests.name: test_any_class
tests.qualityCheck: Tests user-defined and builtin classes and several instance types. It does not enumerate every possible class, which is appropriate for this general rule.
tests.verifies: For each of `type`, `Type`, `type[Any]`, and `Type[Any]`, calls with class arguments `A`, `B`, `C`, `int`, and `str` infer `RB` against an `int` overload; calls with instances `3`, `C()`, and `"s"` also infer `RB` against the corresponding ordinary `int`, `C`, or `str` overload.

tests.evidence: The prompt says `Union` types may appear inside or outside `type[...]`, and that `type[X]` accepts subclasses of `X`; `B` is a subclass of `A`.
tests.name: test_type_of_union
tests.qualityCheck: Covers union annotations inside and outside the type construct, using both a union member and a subclass of a member.
tests.verifies: For each of `type[Union[A, C]]`, `Type[A | C]`, and `type[A] | type[C]` as the second overload, both `f(C)` and `f(B)` infer `RB` rather than the first `int` overload.

tests.evidence: The prompt says that for `type[T]` the provided class must satisfy `T`'s bound or one of its constraints, and that if neither exists any class is accepted. Its class-versus-instance rule and overload-selection/combined-results rules determine the remaining expected results.
tests.name: test_type_of_type_var
tests.qualityCheck: This is a broad matrix for bound, constrained, and unbound TypeVars, including rejected classes, accepted subclasses, and an instance control. The assertions are detailed but track cases expressly described in the prompt.
tests.verifies: With `T` bounded by `A`, `f(C)` with overloads `type[T]`/`int` yields both `RA` and `RB`; `f(C)` against `type[T]`/`type[C]` yields `RB`; `f(B)` and `f(A)` yield `RA`; and `f(B())` against `type[T]`/`A` yields `RB`. With constraints `A, int`, `f(C)` yields `RB`, `f(int)` and `f(B)` yield `RA`, `f(str)` against `type[T]`/`type[str]` yields `RB`, and `f(3)` against `type[T]`/`int` yields `RB`. With unbound `T`, class calls `f(C)` and `f(int)` yield `RA`, while instance call `f(3)` against `type[T]`/`int` yields `RB`.

tests.evidence: The prompt says arguments may be a class name directly or a variable or parameter annotated with `type[...]`.
tests.name: test_type_from_annotated_names
tests.qualityCheck: Exercises both a module-level annotated variable and a function parameter; both return the same selected overload marker.
tests.verifies: Both a variable `t: type[C]` passed as `f(t)` and a parameter `k: type[C]` passed as `f(k)` cause the `type[C]` overload to be selected, producing `RB`.

tests.evidence: The prompt says Jedi identifies the first overload that accepts all arguments and that `type[X]` accepts `X` and its subclasses; it also says bare `type` accepts any class.
tests.name: test_first_matching_overload_wins
tests.qualityCheck: The cases discriminate overload order, overlapping subtype matches, a bare `type` match, and selection after earlier candidates fail.
tests.verifies: For `f(B)` with overloads `type[A]` then `type[B]`, the result is `RA`; reversing those overloads still gives `RA`. With `type[B]` then `type[A]`, `f(A)` gives `RB`. With `type` then `type[A]`, `f(A)` gives `RA`. With overloads `type[A]`, `type[B]`, `type[C]`, `f(C)` gives `RC`.

tests.evidence: The prompt explicitly applies overload selection to keyword arguments and states the relevant class/subclass and class-versus-instance rules.
tests.name: test_type_keyword_argument
tests.qualityCheck: Checks keyword binding for a class, subclass, and instance. The broader multi-parameter and mixed-keyword cases are also exercised in `test_every_argument_has_to_fit`.
tests.verifies: For the single keyword call `f(x=...)`, the `type[C]` overload yields `RB` for `C`, the first `type[A]` overload yields `RA` for `B`, and the ordinary `int` overload yields `RB` for `3`.

tests.evidence: The prompt requires the first overload that accepts *all* arguments, applies the rule to positional and keyword arguments, and says to combine results if no single overload matches.
tests.name: test_every_argument_has_to_fit
tests.qualityCheck: Checks that one incompatible argument disqualifies an overload, that keyword order does not alter binding, and that no-match cases retain both results.
tests.verifies: With `g(x: type[A], y: type[C]) -> RA` and `g(x: type[A], y: type[A]) -> RB`, results are `RA` for `g(A, C)`, `g(B, C)`, and `g(y=C, x=B)`; `RB` for `g(A, A)`, `g(A, y=B)`, and `g(x=A, y=A)`; and both `RA` and `RB` for `g(C, A)` and `g(A, A())`.

tests.evidence: The prompt says annotations on `*args` describe each collected argument, overload selection must account for all arguments, and variadic parameters receiving no arguments count as a match.
tests.name: test_var_positional
tests.qualityCheck: Covers a variadic-only signature and one with a fixed leading parameter, including homogeneous, mixed, and empty collected arguments.
tests.verifies: For both `*x: ...` and `y: int, *x: ...` signatures, `C, C` selects `RB`, `A, B` selects `RA`, `A, C` and `C, A` return both results, and an empty variadic call selects `RA`.

tests.evidence: The prompt explicitly says arguments unpacked at the call site from tuples and lists are taken into account, and specifies per-item annotation behavior for `*args`.
tests.name: test_var_positional_unpacked
tests.qualityCheck: Exercises both tuple and list unpacking with distinct overload-selection outcomes.
tests.verifies: Unpacking tuple `(C, C)` through `f(*ks)` selects `RB`; unpacking list `[A, B]` through `f(*ks)` selects `RA`.

tests.evidence: The prompt says `**kwargs` annotations describe each individual collected argument and that empty variadic parameters count as a match.
tests.name: test_var_keyword
tests.qualityCheck: Checks multiple collected keyword values, a mixed no-match case, both signature shapes, and the empty case.
tests.verifies: For both `**x: ...` and `y: int, **x: ...` signatures, `p=C, q=C` selects `RB`, `p=A, q=B` selects `RA`, `p=A, q=C` returns both results, and an empty collected-keyword call selects `RA`.

tests.evidence: The prompt explicitly says dictionary arguments unpacked at the call site are taken into account, and that `**kwargs` annotations describe each collected argument.
tests.name: test_var_keyword_unpacked
tests.qualityCheck: A direct check of dictionary unpacking; it is a single representative dictionary and value.
tests.verifies: The call `f(**{'p': C})` selects the overload annotated `**x: type[C]`, producing `RB`.

tests.evidence: The prompt specifies TypeVar bound behavior, unions inside `type[...]`, unparameterized `type` accepting any class, per-item variadic annotations, and combined results when no overload matches.
tests.name: test_variadic_parameters_with_other_annotations
tests.qualityCheck: Combines several stated annotation forms with variadic element-by-element matching; it also includes cases where only part of a collected argument sequence fits.
tests.verifies: For `*x: type[T]` with `T` bounded by `A` versus `*x: type[Union[A, C]]`, `f(A, B)` yields `RA`, `f(A, C)` yields `RB`, and `f(C, int)` yields both. For `*x: type` versus `*x: int`, `f(A, int, str)` yields `RA`, `f(A, 1)` yields both, and `f(1, 2)` yields `RB`.

tests.evidence: The prompt applies selection to positional and keyword arguments and to `*args`/`**kwargs`, with each collected value checked against its annotation; it also says empty variadics match and unmatched overload sets combine results.
tests.name: test_variadic_parameters_together
tests.qualityCheck: A useful integration test for fixed parameters, both variadic kinds, a defaulted keyword-capable parameter, and empty collections. The assertions test multiple interactions rather than pinning internal call mechanics.
tests.verifies: For overloads with fixed `y: int`, `*x`, defaulted `z: int`, and `**k`, the results are: `f(1, A, B, p=A)` → `RA`; `f(1, C, z=2, p=C)` → `RB`; `f(1, A, p=C)` → both; `f(1, p=C)` → `RB`; `f(1, C)` → `RB`; and `f(1, z=2)` → `RA`.

tests.evidence: The prompt says to return combined results when no single overload matches, and to select the first overload accepting all supplied arguments when one does.
tests.name: test_no_matching_overload
tests.qualityCheck: Checks both no-match and matching controls, including a variadic call where different elements prevent either overload from accepting the complete argument list.
tests.verifies: For `f(C)` against `type[A]`/`int`, both `RA` and `RB` are returned; for `f(A)`, only `RA` is returned. For variadic `type[A]`/`type[C]`, `f(A, C, int)` returns both results.
